screenings.title: Nil by Mouth
screenings.description: Set in the hardscrabble South London of the filmmaker’s own youth and dedicated—in a more than slightly ambivalent gesture—to the memory of his father, Gary Oldman’s disarmingly raw debut as writer/director/producer flings us into a working-class family’s lives of profane squabbling and substance abuse as lived in the pressure cooker of a council estate flat: tyrannical father Ray (Ray Winstone); long-suffering wife, Val (Kathy Burke); Val’s junkie brother, Billy (Charlie Creed-Miles); Val’s mother and grandmother (Oldman’s sister, billed as Laila Morse, and Edna Doré); and the couple’s young daughter, who has no choice but to soak in the ambient trauma of her surroundings. “Unflinching and observant… There is humor in it, and tender insight… We sense Oldman’s ability to understand, if not forgive.” —Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times

screenings.title: Walkabout
screenings.description: Having fled into the Outback after their father has a psychotic episode that threatens their very lives, two Sydney-bred adolescent siblings (Jenny Agutter and Luc Roeg, the director’s son) meet an Aboriginal teenager (David Gulpilil, in his debut role) on his traditional “walkabout”—a rite-of-passage journey, undertaken in solitude—who aids them in adjusting to the apparently harsh, unforgiving landscape around them, a landscape that, as Walkabout progresses, is heavily romanticised, revealing an Edenic splendor lurking beneath its sun-baked surface. A foundational text of the Australian New Wave and a film of genuinely awe-striking natural beauty, shot by cinematographer-turned-director Roeg himself.

screenings.title: The Same River Twice
screenings.description: “A piercingly poignant then-and-now portrait of five friends who worked as summer guides on the Colorado River in the 1970’s... so palpable it puts a lump in your throat.” – Stephen Holden, The New York Times “Powerful... Compelling... Graceful... Part of what makes THE SAME RIVER TWICE great is its highly selective and shaped methods of portraying the individuals, almost as if they were fictional creations. The way in which the present gradually overtakes the past in this film is more evidence of Moss’ flawless sense of narrative construction.” – Jonathan Rosenbaum, Chicago Reader “Beguiling, lyrical portrait of idealism and adulthood.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “Graceful... Fluid and loose... THE SAME RIVER TWICE will exert the same alluring pull as Michael Apted’s 7 UP and other where-are-they-now investigations into the passage of real lives.” – Ella Taylor, LA Weekly “It's a generous document of cultural passage, and not incidentally, the sexiest naturally nudist American movie since Murnau’s TABU.” – Michael Atkinson, The Village Voice “Other documentaries have crisscrossed between time frames, but Moss’ beguiling THE SAME RIVER TWICE represents one of the most effective uses of the device.” – Kevin Thomas, Los Angeles Times “An elegy, an allegory, and one hell of a beautiful film.” – Walter Chaw, Film Freak Central

screenings.title: The Untouchables
screenings.description: Dir. Brian De Palma. 1987, 119 mins. 70mm. With Kevin Costner, Sean Connery, Charles Martin Smith, Andy García, Robert De Niro. Master craftsman De Palma collaborated with playwright David Mamet to adapt the 1950s ABC television series—itself an adaptation of Elliot Ness’s autobiography—into one of the great cinematic achievements of the 1980s. In the performance that helped launch him to stardom, Costner plays Ness, a lawman in Prohibition-era Chicago tracking notorious criminal kingpin Al Capone (De Niro), whose net of influence over the city extends to officers in Ness’s own department. He teams with a fearless veteran Irish cop (Connery, in an Oscar-winning performance) and principled Italian American rookie (Garcia) to pursue justice in the face of overwhelming criminality and corruption. Never one to shy away from a challenge, De Palma shoots the hell out of The Untouchables, assisting universally strong performances with majestic framing, virtuosic movement, and undaunted violence. And yes, during an elaborate showdown in Chicago’s Union Station, he directly apes the Odessa Steps sequence from Eisenstein’s Potemkin—one of the best-known scenes in the history of cinema—not as a winking homage, but with the confidence that he can exceed it. screenings.title: Union County
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass
screenings.description: Small town hairdresser Gail Daughtry is engaged to her devoted high school sweetheart, Tom. Her life takes a turn when a trip to a book signing leads to Tom meeting – and sleeping – with his “celebrity pass”. Reeling from the betrayal, Gail impulsively joins her friend Otto on a trip to Los Angeles, where a psychic convinces Gail that the only way to save her marriage is to “even the scales” with her own celebrity pass: Jon Hamm. Thus begins an epic journey through Tinseltown as Gail and Otto join forces with a talent agency assistant, a paparazzo, and actor John Slattery, all in the search for Hamm. Along the way, they collide with celebrities and are hunted by a group of Italian assassins as they get ever closer to finding the elusive star.
screenings.country: Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass Comedy

screenings.title: Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing
screenings.description: An investigative documentary that explores the deepening corporate crisis and systemic safety failures at Boeing, following the fatal 737 MAX crashes and the tragic death of whistleblower John Barnett.

screenings.title: White Nights
screenings.description: Italy, 1957 Directed by Luchino Visconti Based on the short story by Fyodor Dostoevsky Starring Marcello Mastroianni, Maria Schell, Jean Marais Music by Nino Rota In Italian with English subtitles Approx 103 min. “Visconti’s version of the Dostoevsky story—about the chance encounter of a couple as she is waiting in vain for her lover, and the obsessive, panic-stricken relationship which then develops between them—later filmed by Bresson as FOUR NIGHTS OF A DREAMER. Visconti traps his characters (three excellent performances) within a claustrophobic canal-side set, and the film is a series of brief walks, chases, attempted escapes, always frustrated. Shot as neo-realist high tragedy, the film offers its characters only one strange moment of escape from their night-time obsessions—a raucous, sexual, subversive scene in a dance-hall. Then the snow comes down, and with it a chilly desperation about the extent of human self-delusion.” – Time Out Restored by Luce Cinecittà, from the original 35mm negative Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: Portals and Fluids: a Celebration with Shu Lea Cheang (w/q&a) (w/q&a)
screenings.description: Shu Lea Cheang’s new work LOVER LOVE, a commission by the Leslie-Lohman Museum of Art, has taken up residency in the museum since April. The mammoth work is both highly immersive and highly interactive; moveable screens serve as portals into Shu Lea Cheang’s unmistakable transhumanist worldview. The digital and physical collide in a blooming dream of gender non-conforming utopia. On the occasion of Cheang’s visit to New York this August, Spectacle is thrilled to welcome the artist (whose IKU was a midnight favorite at the theater in 2017) for a one-of-a-kind presentation of cyberpunk queer futures.

screenings.title: Gypsy 83: The Director’s Cut
screenings.description: Sandusky, Ohio is hell on earth for goth misfits and Stevie Nicks superfans Gypsy Vale (Sara Rue) and her younger, queer protégée Clive Webb (Birkett Turton). When they discover a New York City club is hosting a “Night of 1000 Stevies”, the pair hit the road with high hopes that Gypsy will be able to perform. Along the way, they encounter other misfits who pave the way to their salvation, all while discovering profound truths about themselves. Costarring John Doe of the legendary punk band X and the great Karen Black as a has-been lounge singer, Todd Stephens’s cult favorite puts a queer, outsider spin on both the road movie and the coming-of-age journey, with plenty of black eyeliner to spare.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Center Stage
screenings.description: Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Stanley Kwan Starring Maggie Cheung, Han Chin, Carina Lau, Tony Leung Ka-fai In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English Approx. 155 min. International superstar Maggie Cheung (IN THE MOOD FOR LOVE) embodies tragic screen siren Ruan Lingyu, known as the “Greta Garbo of China,” in this unconventional biopic by Hong Kong New Wave master Stanley Kwan (ROUGE). Praised for her moving and emotive onscreen presence, Ruan’s private life, which was frequent fodder for the vicious Shanghai tabloids, began to mirror the melodramas which brought her fame, culminating in her suicide at age 24. Kwan and Cheung paint a kaleidoscopic yet intimate portrait of the ill-fated actress, deftly blending lush period drama, archival footage, and metatextual documentary sequences of Cheung reflecting on Ruan’s legacy. The result is, much like the films of Ruan Lingyu themselves, “tender, vivid, and almost overwhelmingly moving” (Time Out). Presented by Fortune Star Media Limited, the restoration of the film was carried out from the original 35mm picture and optical soundtrack negative. The prints were repaired, cleaned and scanned in Hong Kong, then digitally restored in 4K resolution in Bologna, Italy by L'Immagine Ritrovata. Endorsed by the director, Stanley Kwan, the color correction was completed by Interface Video Production Ltd in Hong Kong. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: I Love You and I’ll Take You to the Movies
The Hunger
screenings.description: A lush vampire romance with sex and style to spare, much of it provided by stars Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as a couple of posh, centuries-old nightclubbing New York bloodsuckers who, when one begins to show the first signs of aging, recruit assistance from Susan Sarandon’s geriatrics researcher, then find themselves in a very, very attractive throuple. Yes, that’s “Bela Lugosi’s Dead” artists Bauhaus in a brief cameo.

screenings.title: Obsession
screenings.description: De Palma’s twisted twist on Hitchcock’s Vertigo stars Cliff Robertson as a wealthy New Orleans real-estate developer still mourning the loss of his beloved wife (Dead Ringers’ Genevieve Bujold) and daughter years after their abductions until, on a visit to Florence, he encounters her exact double. (In addition to Hitch, screenwriter Paul Schrader drew inspiration from Dante and his infatuation with muse Beatrice.) With lusciously gauzy cinematography by Vilmos Zsigmond, a richly romantic score by Hitch regular Bernard Herrmann, and Big Easy Baroque location shooting, this is moviemaking as ultrarich confection, a swooning transport “to a more romantic era… and the simple, touching pleasures denied the audience by the current antiromantic spirit of the movies” [Richard Schickel].

screenings.title: Dead Souls
screenings.description: In 1890, the year of the U.S. census, chaos erupts when a stranger named Strindler arrives in a small town in Arizona and requests money for providing the names of dead Mexican laborers. Adapted from the novel by Nikolai Gogol.

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: Willem Dafoe is Ed Saxberger, a postal worker whose former life as a downtown poet in late-70s New York is rediscovered by a young admirer (Donovan) and his “Enthusiasm Society,” a group of 20-somethings with a comically romanticized sense of the past. In the company of his new friends, including the mysterious and mercurial Gloria (Lee of PAST LIVES), Ed has the uncanny feeling of merging with his younger self. Directed by Kent Jones (DIANE) from a witty, razor-sharp script by Samy Burch (MAY DECEMBER), LATE FAME is a funny, lively, poignant, and occasionally haunting New York story. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film 2025 96 MIN. USA MAGNOLIA PICTURES

screenings.title: Dread Beat an Blood
screenings.description: About DREAD BEAT AN BLOOD: “[A] gem... a portrait of the artist as principled activist.” – Sasha Frere-Jones, 4Columns “Fantastic... An amazing snapshot of the time of the pre-Brixton riots... This is so relevant a movie. That’s what makes it so good.” – Gilles Peterson, BBC “A fascinating document of LKJ in his time and place, touring with the sound systems, strolling through the market and visiting Tulse Hill schools, vividly capturing black British culture in a country on the cusp of Thatcherism, just a few months before the Brixton uprising.” – Stephen Troussé, Uncut “An invaluable document of Brixton, an area that was already at the front lines of the anti-racist struggle, the streets in which people would soon rise up in rebellion. That sense of latent frustration simmers in every frame. It is Johnson himself who articulates that frustration, honing that anger into art via his poetry.” – Kevin Mccaighy, The Quietus About Linton Kwesi Johnson: “If any young artists need to know about longevity and integrity, Linton Kwesi Johnson is the one to look to... He knew his path and he walked it. His words are still relevant and that reggae bass is still vibrating.” – Steve McQueen “Linton Kwesi Johnson’s impact on the cultural landscape over the last half-century has been colossal and multi-generational.” – The Guardian “He’s written the anthems for a generation who felt oppressed and victimized... He’s now celebrated as one of this country’s most influential cultural commentators.” – BBC “A revolutionary poet for our times.” – Jacobin “The Poet Laureate of Black Britain.” – Paul Gilroy “The roots of hip-hop run deep, and among the deepest branches remains Linton Kwesi Johnson, the Jamaican-born, British-raised poet, writer, and performer often hailed as the father of dub poetry.” – David Browne, Rolling Stone

screenings.title: Train to Busan
screenings.description: Yeon Sang-ho’s global phenomenon TRAIN TO BUSAN arrives back in theaters to celebrate its 10th Anniversary. What begins as a simple birthday trip for a father and daughter turns into a high-octane fight for survival when a zombie outbreak ravages South Korea. Trapped on a speeding train, they must navigate a landscape of terror to reach safety. Experience the relentless action and heart-wrenching drama on the big screen like never before.

screenings.title: Sheila and the Brainstem
screenings.description: SURFER, a film directed, acted, scored, and shot by Douglas Burke and Burke International Pictures, might have an answer to this question. At turns a Californian mystic experience, a Biblical parable, and very nearly an adventure thriller, it is at its heart a sort of SURF REFORMED, where men approach faith with the help of the supernatural. Burke approaches the camera like the rhythms of the ocean, nodding to both YouTube how-to videos and Béla Tarr in the same rolling beat. He is less interested in getting the camera tripod out of the shot than he is in the elusive and crucial process of finding one’s élan vital. The waves of destiny grow bigger with each return to the water, as images of surfers guide our hero to his ultimate challenge. Will the teen confront fear? We intuitively know the answer.

screenings.title: Chungking Express
screenings.description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking.

screenings.title: Irreversible
screenings.description: Fourteen long sequence shots arranged in reverse chronology take us on a journey from hell to heaven, from nightmarish violence to connubial bliss. In a BDSM club evocatively called Club Rectum, Pierre (Albert Dupontel) dashes in the face of a man who’s just broken the arm of his friend, Marcus (Vincent Cassel), and is preparing to rape him. From this memorable cold open, we see the events leading up to this bloody denouement—an evening that begins (or ends, as it were) as an innocent outing by the two friends and Marcus’s girlfriend, Alex (Monica Bellucci). Not a film to leave the viewer indifferent, to put it very mildly, featuring a positively punitive, bowel-churning soundtrack by Daft Punk’s Thomas Bangalter.

screenings.title: Manson Family Movies
screenings.description: Between the years of 1974 to 1979, not long after Manson Family trials had concluded, enigmatic artist and connoisseur of fringe culture, John Aes-Nihil, embarked on a project to “re-stage” the events leading up to the infamous Tate-LaBianca murders as a series of faux home movies, based on the legend that the Family had at one point stolen camera equipment to document their actions. The resulting feature— which, coincidentally, premiered in 1984 at EZTV alongside HIGHWAY HYPNOSIS— truly lives up to its filmmaker’s namesake Aesthetic Nihilism: Shot entirely on Super8mm and completely silent save for an accompanying soundtrack mostly comprised of music made by the Family itself (plus a little Patty Duke for good measure). The film re-frames the Manson Family story as a first-person travelogue across Southern California, imbued with chillingly realistic detail as we bear (false) witness to one of the most notorious events of the American century.

screenings.title: The Birdcage
screenings.description: In this remake of the classic French farce La Cage aux Folles, engaged couple Val Goldman (Dan Futterman) and Barbara Keeley (Calista Flockhart) shakily introduce their future in-laws. Val’s father, Armand (Robin Williams), a gay Miami drag club owner, pretends to be straight and attempts to hide his relationship with Albert (Nathan Lane), his life partner and the club’s flamboyant star attraction, so as to please Barbara’s father, controversial Republican Sen. Kevin Keeley (Gene Hackman).

screenings.title: Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing
screenings.description: An investigative documentary that explores the deepening corporate crisis and systemic safety failures at Boeing, following the fatal 737 MAX crashes and the tragic death of whistleblower John Barnett.

screenings.title: The Dark Knight
screenings.description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.”

screenings.title: A Day in the Country + People on Sunday
screenings.director: Robert Siodmak, Jean Renoir , Edgar G. Ulmer
screenings.description: Two slices of life from Europe entre deux guerres, and two compact masterpieces. Renoir’s featurette fragment, based on a Guy de Maupassant short story and only edited 10 years after its shoot came to a premature end, evokes the disappeared world of Belle Époque France—the world of Renoir’s father, the painter Pierre-Auguste—by describing an afternoon’s outing for two young shirt-chasers, a middle-aged Paris shopkeeper, and the shopkeeper’s susceptible-to-flattery wife and daughter. People on Sunday, made by a supergroup brain trust of future cinematic luminaries including Billy Wilder, Fred Zinnemann, Robert Siodmak, and Edgar G. Ulmer, follows a quintet of Berliners through a weekend of walks along the Wannsee, domestic squabbles, and frisky flirtation. Modest in ambition, yet they contain the world in miniature.

screenings.title: Lawrence of Arabia (70mm)
screenings.description: Screening added 8/21 by popular demand Dir. David Lean. 1962, 227 mins. (plus intermission). U.S. 70mm. With Peter O’Toole, Omar Sharif, Alec Guinness, Anthony Quinn. The apex of David Lean’s magnificent career was this unparalleled spectacle which won seven Oscars, including Best Picture. Lawrence of Arabia rocketed Peter O’Toole to stardom as real-life adventurer T. E. Lawrence, a former British officer whose expedition to Cairo in 1916 leads him to side with the Arabs against the Turks, eventually organizing his own guerrilla army. With its overwhelming widescreen desert vistas, this is one of cinema’s most transporting experiences, a film that all but demands the big-screen treatment. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Please note: The 8/15 and 8/23 screenings are sold out. Standby tickets may become available at the door on the evening of the event. Purchase tickets for Friday, 8/21 at 6:00 p.m.

screenings.title: CatVideoFest 2026
screenings.description: 2026, 70 mins. DCP. The cats came back! CatVideoFest returns for 2026 with a compilation of the latest and best cat videos culled from countless hours of unique submissions and sourced animations, music videos, and classic internet powerhouses. Each year, across the country, local theaters partner with nearby cat-focused charities, animal welfare associations and shelters alike—a portion of ticket proceeds from every show goes directly to local cats in need. This year we are partnering with Catstoria Cat Rescue. An Oscilloscope Laboratories release. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / discounted for MoMI members ($7–$11). There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Purchase tickets for the screening on August 8 at 1:00 p.m. Purchase tickets for the screening on August 9 at 1:00 p.m. Purchase tickets for the screening on August 9 at 3:00 p.m. Purchase tickets for the screening on August 15 at 2:00 p.m. Purchase tickets for the screening on August 16 at 1:00 p.m. Purchase tickets for the screening on August. 16 at 4:00 p.m. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Barrio Triste
screenings.description: Medellin, 1987. A group of teen outcasts steals a news camera to document every detail of their dangerous lives. The first feature from acclaimed photographer and Bad Bunny music video director Stillz redefines the found footage genre as a haunting, poignant coming-of-age story with a disturbing twist. Set to an awe-inspiring score by Arca and produced by Harmony Korine’s collective EDGLRD, the film taps into the anxieties of a youth culture from the margins of history yearning to be understood.
screenings.country: Barrio Triste Crime, Drama, Fantasy, Horror

screenings.title: Two by Robb Moss
screenings.description: A pair of films from Moss, a master of first-person documentary and longtime Professor at Harvard’s Department of Art, Film, and Visual Studies, who will join Metrograph for the screening. Riverdogs is Moss’s lyrical, beautifully photographed account of a 35-day trek down the Colorado River, a paean to youth, the natural world, and a fleeting moment in the increasingly distant past. In his confessional The Tourist, Moss meditates—with a wry sense of humor—on the early years of his marriage, his failed attempts to start a family with his new wife, and the daily vicissitudes of professional life as an itinerant freelance cameraman.

screenings.title: Deliverance
screenings.description: A quartet of city slicker businessman buddies (Jon Voight, Ned Beatty, Ronny Cox and, in a star-making role, Burt Reynolds) leave Atlanta to head into the Georgia backwoods for what’s meant to be a little weekend canoe trip… and stumble headlong instead into the hidden horrors lurking in the old Southland. The trial-by-fire endurance test that they’ll pass through makes for pure, pulse-pounding cinema, with at least three scenes—the “Dueling Banjos” gas station stop, Beatty’s “Squeal like a pig!” humiliation, and the white-water rapids set piece—that rank above the most remembered in ’70s American cinema.

screenings.title: Black Book | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: After narrowly escaping death, young Rachel Rosenthal (Carice van Houten) becomes part of the Jewish resistance, assuming the name Ellis de Vries. Her superiors order her to seduce a Gestapo officer named Ludwig (Sebastian Koch). Ellis is successful in her mission but soon finds herself falling in love with her mortal enemy.

screenings.title: The Walker
screenings.description: A highly engaging and dynamic exploration of artist Humberto Castro’s personal life, as well as the Neofigurative aesthetics that define his work.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Hannibal
screenings.description: Hopkins reprises his role from 1991’s The Silence of the Lambs as psychiatrist-turned-cannibal serial killer Hannibal Lecter in Scott’s follow-up, a gristly fairy tale that finds FBI special agent Clarice Starling (Julianne Moore, ably taking on the role originated by Jodie Foster) racing against time to find to catch up with her old foil before he’s located by Mason R. Verger (Gary Oldman), a sadistic scion of enormous wealth who, after years earlier being grotesquely mutilated by Lecter, has dedicated the entirety of his power and influence towards a terrible and extravagant dream of vengeance. Unidentified in promotional materials and unbilled until the film’s closing credits, wholly unrecognizable under a prosthetic mask, and stripped of almost every expressive tool an actor traditionally relies upon to practice their craft, Oldman offers up an indelible portrayal of utter and absolute human corruption.

screenings.title: Nil by Mouth
screenings.description: Set in the hardscrabble South London of the filmmaker’s own youth and dedicated—in a more than slightly ambivalent gesture—to the memory of his father, Gary Oldman’s disarmingly raw debut as writer/director/producer flings us into a working-class family’s lives of profane squabbling and substance abuse as lived in the pressure cooker of a council estate flat: tyrannical father Ray (Ray Winstone); long-suffering wife, Val (Kathy Burke); Val’s junkie brother, Billy (Charlie Creed-Miles); Val’s mother and grandmother (Oldman’s sister, billed as Laila Morse, and Edna Doré); and the couple’s young daughter, who has no choice but to soak in the ambient trauma of her surroundings. “Unflinching and observant… There is humor in it, and tender insight… We sense Oldman’s ability to understand, if not forgive.” —Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times

screenings.title: Challengers
screenings.description: Dir. Luca Guadagnino. 2024, 131 mins. U.S. DCP with Dolby Atmos. With Zendaya, Josh O’Connor, Mike Faist. This scintillating, sexy tennis drama follows a trio of characters whose mercurial relationship blurs the line between love triangle and throuple. Close friends and doubles partners, Patrick (O’Connor) and Art (Faist) find their dynamic irreversibly changed the moment tennis prodigy Tashi Duncan (Zendaya) enters their lives as teenagers. Several years and one career-ending injury later, Tashi finds herself coaching (and married to) one of the romantic rivals as he prepares to face off with his former best friend, culminating in a tennis match with more at stake than mere points. Featuring wildly expressive cinematography by Sayombhu Mukdeeprom, a cleverly structured script by Justin Kuritzkes, and a breathtaking, kinetic score by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / discounted for MoMI members ($7–$11). There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. screenings.description: A female playwright explores the Cuban exodus through real-life testimonies of their experiences in countries all over the globe, including Iceland, Spain, and Angola. ADIÓS CUBA resonates strongly with today’s immigrant crisis worldwide.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass
screenings.description: Small town hairdresser Gail Daughtry is engaged to her devoted high school sweetheart, Tom. Her life takes a turn when a trip to a book signing leads to Tom meeting – and sleeping – with his “celebrity pass”. Reeling from the betrayal, Gail impulsively joins her friend Otto on a trip to Los Angeles, where a psychic convinces Gail that the only way to save her marriage is to “even the scales” with her own celebrity pass: Jon Hamm. Thus begins an epic journey through Tinseltown as Gail and Otto join forces with a talent agency assistant, a paparazzo, and actor John Slattery, all in the search for Hamm. Along the way, they collide with celebrities and are hunted by a group of Italian assassins as they get ever closer to finding the elusive star.
screenings.country: Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass Comedy

screenings.title: The Others
screenings.description: Having enjoyed a palpable international hit with his Abre Los Ojos—picked up for an American remake, under the title Vanilla Sky, by Tom Cruise—Amenábar made his English-language debut with The Others, a dolorous, deftly directed Old Dark House chiller set in the immediate aftermath of World War II, about a devoutly religious Englishwoman (Nicole Kidman, superb) living in a remote home in the Channel Island with her two young, severely photosensitive children and the strange goings-on that begin shortly after she takes on a trio of new servants. “Elegant… Creates more tension from atmosphere alone than most other horror films do from vats full of fake blood.” —The Times of London

screenings.title: Four Adventures of Reinette and Mirabelle
screenings.description: Shot quickly in and around Paris during a production break on Rohmer’s Le Rayon Vert, this breezy, witty film traces the exploits of two young women—one an ethnology student from the city, the other an unsophisticated aspiring artist from the country. Reinette and Mirabelle (played by Joëlle Miquel and Jessica Forde) become instant friends upon meeting in the first of four vignettes that make up the film (“The Blue Hour”), and in their first two days together, they decide to become roommates in Paris. Throughout the three remaining stories, they encounter many of the inevitable characters of a modern city: the impossible waiter (“The Waiter”), the Metro-station hustler (“The Beggar, the Kleptomaniac and the Hustler”), and the snooty gallery owner (“Selling the Painting”). A Metrograph Pictures release

screenings.title: The Jungle Book
screenings.description: Inspired by the adventures of the foundling Mowgli in Rudyard Kipling’s 1894 collection of the same name, The Jungle Book—the final animated Disney feature to be overseen in its production by Uncle Walt—would become one of the studio’s biggest hits, thanks in no small part to its exceptional confluence of vocal talent (yes, that’s George Sanders as the suavely sinister Bengal tiger Shere Khan) and unforgettable songbook, including perennial favorites “The Bare Necessities” and “I Wanna Be Like You (The Monkey Song),” the latter volcanically belted out by none other than jump blues howler extraordinaire Louis Prima. Brisk, breezy, and simply buckets of fun.

screenings.title: The Birdcage
screenings.description: In this remake of the classic French farce La Cage aux Folles, engaged couple Val Goldman (Dan Futterman) and Barbara Keeley (Calista Flockhart) shakily introduce their future in-laws. Val’s father, Armand (Robin Williams), a gay Miami drag club owner, pretends to be straight and attempts to hide his relationship with Albert (Nathan Lane), his life partner and the club’s flamboyant star attraction, so as to please Barbara’s father, controversial Republican Sen. Kevin Keeley (Gene Hackman).

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: In future Britain, Alex DeLarge, a charismatic and psychopath delinquent, who likes to practice crimes and ultra-violence with his gang, is jailed and volunteers for an experimental aversion therapy developed by the government in an effort to solve society's crime problem - but not all goes according to plan. Cast Malcolm McDowell Patrick Magee Michael Bates Warren Clarke John Clive Adrienne Corri Carl Duering Paul Farrell Clive Francis Michael Gover

screenings.title: Walkabout
screenings.description: Having fled into the Outback after their father has a psychotic episode that threatens their very lives, two Sydney-bred adolescent siblings (Jenny Agutter and Luc Roeg, the director’s son) meet an Aboriginal teenager (David Gulpilil, in his debut role) on his traditional “walkabout”—a rite-of-passage journey, undertaken in solitude—who aids them in adjusting to the apparently harsh, unforgiving landscape around them, a landscape that, as Walkabout progresses, is heavily romanticised, revealing an Edenic splendor lurking beneath its sun-baked surface. A foundational text of the Australian New Wave and a film of genuinely awe-striking natural beauty, shot by cinematographer-turned-director Roeg himself.

screenings.title: Otar Iosseliani Early Shorts Program
screenings.description: A program of the inspired early shorts that established Iosseliani at the forefront of a new, rising generation of Georgian filmmakers. Featuring Akvarel, in which a quarreling working-class couple experience a revelation at an art exhibition; Sapovnela, in which an old man who tends exquisite flower gardens in the hills around Mtskheta sees his life’s work threatened by the arrival of a new road; April, in which a young couple find their happiness dwindling as their comfort increases upon moving into a brand new, squeaky clean housing development, and Tudzhi (Cast Iron), a documentary description of life in an ironworks that singles out individuals on the factory floor not as symbols of thrumming Soviet industrial might, but as human beings.

screenings.title: Jaws
screenings.description: Please note: The screening on Friday, August 21 has been canceled. Tickets are available for the screenings on August 16 and August 22. Screening in Dolby Atmos Dir. Steven Spielberg. U.S., 1975, 124 mins. DCP with Dolby Atmos. With Roy Scheider, Robert Shaw, Richard Dreyfuss, Lorraine Gary. The summer movie that started it all, this improbable, against-all-odds blockbuster about a New England vacation spot terrorized by a great white shark proved that Steven Spielberg was a force to be reckoned with. Adapting Peter Benchley’s hit novel, not only did he compose a technical masterpiece of Hitchcockian suspense by ingeniously working around an unwieldy rubber prop, he created an exhilarating film of existential horror that kept millions away from the beach. And with Scheider, Shaw, and Dreyfuss, he gave audiences a trio of unforgettable adventurers who, in great seventies fashion, went against the grain of American macho. For better or for worse, American cinema was never the same again. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / free for MoMI members at the Senior/Student level and above. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets for Sunday, August 16 Order tickets for Saturday, August 22 Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: CatVideoFest 2026
screenings.description: 2026, 70 mins. DCP. The cats came back! CatVideoFest returns for 2026 with a compilation of the latest and best cat videos culled from countless hours of unique submissions and sourced animations, music videos, and classic internet powerhouses. Each year, across the country, local theaters partner with nearby cat-focused charities, animal welfare associations and shelters alike—a portion of ticket proceeds from every show goes directly to local cats in need. This year we are partnering with Catstoria Cat Rescue. An Oscilloscope Laboratories release. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / discounted for MoMI members ($7–$11). There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Falling Leaves
screenings.description: Iosseliani’s debut feature—winner of the FIPRESCI Award at Cannes—follows newly minted oenologists Nico and Otar, just out of winemaking school, as they head to work at an agricultural cooperative in Tbilisi, there to have their first intimate experiences of the opposite sex… as well as their introduction to the corruption bred by stifling bureaucracy and arbitrarily imposed production quotas. A stinging satire of Soviet-style economic planning and its unintended consequences smuggled within a pseudo-documentary depiction of the Georgian wine industry, and a deeply personal film about youth for the first time facing up to the full measure of adult negligence and corruption.

screenings.title: 54: The Director's Cut + Q&A | This is Cinématographe
screenings.description: New York City, 1979: working class Jersey City teenager Shane (Ryan Phillippe, Cruel Intentions) becomes infatuated with Studio 54, a lavish Manhattan nightclub known for decadence. Shane’s time at 54 introduces him to a cast of characters including real life nightclub owner Steve Rubell (Mike Myers, Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery), busboy Greg (Breckin Meyer, Clueless), coat checker Anita (Salma Hayek, Traffic), and actress Julie (Neve Campbell, Scream).

screenings.title: Paranoid Park
screenings.description: Adapting Blake Nelson’s Y.A. novel of the same name, Van Sant renders the youth gathering place of the skate park a voluptuous dreamscape with the help of cinematographers Chris Doyle and Rain Kathy Li. Teenaged skate rat Alex—Gabe Nevins, leading a largely amateur cast recruited via MySpace—finds himself a prime suspect in the death of a security guard, silently carrying a crushing burden of knowledge through his daily rounds, a contrast to the gravity-defying liberation he finds carving it up at “Paranoid Park.”

screenings.description: An investigative documentary that explores the deepening corporate crisis and systemic safety failures at Boeing, following the fatal 737 MAX crashes and the tragic death of whistleblower John Barnett.

screenings.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (70mm)
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1968, 149 mins (plus intermission). U.S. 70mm. With Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood. As brilliantly engineered as the space program itself, Stanley Kubrick’s mysterious and profound sci-fi epic—“the ultimate trip”—is about nothing less than the beauty and the banality of civilization, blending cool satire, an elaborate vision of the future, and passages of avant-garde cinematic inventiveness. Set in a future that is already the past, 2001 envisions space travel as both hilariously routine and mind-bending, a journey to the infinite and beyond that forever changed the way we see the universe and cinema itself. As experienced on 70mm in MoMI’s Redstone Theater, Kubrick’s surreal masterwork still has the ability to conduct viewers to untold, unknowable realms of artistry and daring. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Please note: The Saturday, August 8 screening is sold out. Limited tickets may become available at the door on standby. Buy tickets for 8/16 Buy tickets for 8/28 Buy tickets for 8/30

screenings.title: There Once Was a Singing Blackbird
screenings.description: Gia (Gela Kandelaki), a timpanist in the Tbilisi Philharmonic, has made a science of getting to work just on time to hit his lone cue and then dashing out the door, so as to leave the rest of his hours open for sweet-talking women and carousing with pals. A marvelous character study of an open-handed, incurably impulsive young man infected by the bustling, on-the-go energy of the city around him, and a film that careens along with the same freewheeling spontaneity displayed by its protagonist. Screens with Georgian Ancient Songs, which Iosseliani described thusly: “It’s a film about Georgian traditional polyphony. Georgian songs are always sung in one, two, three or even four voices. It’s a story about how these songs are structured. And at the same time we show what life was like in the old days. The official reaction to the film was one of indignation. I managed to steal a print of the film and keep it safe.”

screenings.title: The Milk of Sorrow
screenings.description: Winner of the Golden Bear at the 59th Berlin International Film Festival, Llosa’s formidable sophomore feature focuses on Fausta (Magaly Solier, in a performance nearly free of dialogue), the only daughter of an aged Indigenous Peruvian woman who, following her mother’s death, must negotiate arrangements for her burial as well as negotiate the smothering legacy of trauma that her parent, horribly misused during the Shining Path terrorist insurgencies of the 1980s and ’90s, has left behind with her child even after herself departing this mortal coil. “Littered with unforgettable images of incongruity, destruction, and, finally, healing” [The Village Voice], The Milk of Sorrow is an exquisitely shot study in inherited injury guarded like a precious heirloom, a work of tragic magic realism.

screenings.title: The Fountain | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: As a modern-day scientist, Tommy is struggling with mortality, desperately searching for the medical breakthrough that will save the life of his cancer-stricken wife, Izzi.

screenings.title: Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing
screenings.description: An investigative documentary that explores the deepening corporate crisis and systemic safety failures at Boeing, following the fatal 737 MAX crashes and the tragic death of whistleblower John Barnett.

screenings.title: Comandante Fritz
screenings.description: In this tongue-in-cheek comedy, East German Stasi officer Fritz travels to Cuba with orders to thwart a suspected CIA operation against Fidel Castro. In Havana he meets Lola, a young woman who changes the course of his life.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: La Notte
screenings.description: Novelist Giovanni Pontano (Marcello Mastroianni) is the toast of the Italian literary scene, but smothered by the trappings of success. His misery weighs heavily on his wife, Lidia (Jeanne Moreau), already carrying her own cargo of existential anguish. In the course of a day and a night—spent at a hospital sickroom, a book launch, a nightclub, and a party at an industrialist’s villa, where Giovanni flirts extensively with the host’s daughter, Valentina (Monica Vitti)—the couple must come to terms with the extinction of the love that once existed between them… or not? A film steeped in despair but thrilling in its adventurous, architectonic use of the cinematic medium, from its opening credits—an avant-jazz/musique concrète overture accompanying the industrialized Milanese cityscape—to its beguiling final scene.

screenings.title: Les Bonnes Femmes
screenings.description: An early and enormous artistic triumph of the French New Wave, Chabrol’s quietly class-conscious film records the dreams, dramas, and self-deceptions of a quartet of young Parisian girls working at an appliance shop, among them Bernadette Lafont and Stéphane Audran. A study of the social habits of the petite bourgeoisie, set against indubitably authentic locations seen in crisp black-and-white courtesy DP Henri Decaë, which develops into a melancholy cautionary tale on the risks of romantic illusion.

screenings.title: Incorrectional: A Memorial Service
screenings.description: Incorrectional: A Memorial Service is both a film screening and a last hurrah. Due to a years-long legal battle, the film must be removed from circulation and any remaining prints, screeners, files, and elements are to be destroyed as per an agreement between private entities and the filmmaking team. What will transpire will be a screening of the film and a memorial service where the creative team and any appreciators (programmers, critics, observers) will give an oral remembrance and/or dedication. After tributes are given, the project files will be deleted in front of the audience, and the project hard drive will be destroyed. Funeral attire is recommended.

screenings.title: Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing
screenings.description: An investigative documentary that explores the deepening corporate crisis and systemic safety failures at Boeing, following the fatal 737 MAX crashes and the tragic death of whistleblower John Barnett.

screenings.title: Chungking Express
screenings.description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking.

screenings.title: The Hunger
screenings.description: A lush vampire romance with sex and style to spare, much of it provided by stars Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as a couple of posh, centuries-old nightclubbing New York bloodsuckers who, when one begins to show the first signs of aging, recruit assistance from Susan Sarandon’s geriatrics researcher, then find themselves in a very, very attractive throuple. Yes, that’s “Bela Lugosi’s Dead” artists Bauhaus in a brief cameo.

screenings.title: Europa Europa
screenings.description: As World War II splits Europe, sixteen-year-old German Jew Salomon (Marco Hofschneider) is separated from his family after fleeing with them to Poland, and finds himself reluctantly assuming various ideological identities in order to hide the deadly secret of his Jewishness. He is bounced from a Soviet orphanage, where he plays a dutiful Stalinist, to the Russian front, where he hides in plain sight as an interpreter for the German army, and back to his home country, where he takes on his most dangerous role: a member of the Hitler Youth. Based on the real-life experiences of Salomon Perel, Agnieszka Holland’s wartime tour de force Europa Europa is a breathless survival story told with the verve of a comic adventure, an ironic refutation of the Nazi idea of racial purity, and a complex portrait of a young man caught up in shifting historical calamities and struggling to stay alive. In German, Russian, Polish, Hebrew and Yiddish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Crank | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: The hit-man Chev Chelios is poisoned by the criminal Verona and his friend and doctor Miles advises him that he must keep his adrenaline in an upper level to stay alive. Chev meets his girlfriend Eve and together he looks for Verona to kill him.

screenings.title: Green Border
screenings.description: In the treacherous and swampy forests that make up the so-called “green border” between Belarus and Poland, refugees from the Middle East and Africa are lured by government propaganda promising easy passage to the European Union. Unable to cross into Europe and unable to turn back, they find themselves trapped in a rapidly escalating geopolitical stand-off. An unflinching depiction of the migrant crisis captured in stark black-and-white, this riveting film explores the intractable issue from multiple perspectives: a Syrian family fleeing ISIS caught between cruel border guards in both countries; young guards instructed to brutalize and reject the migrants; and activists who aid the refugees at great personal risk. Holland brings a masterful eye for realism and deep compassion to this blistering critique of a humanitarian calamity that continues to unfold. Winner of the Special Jury Prize at the 2023 Venice Film Festival. In Polish, Arabic, English and French with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Dead Souls
screenings.description: In 1890, the year of the U.S. census, chaos erupts when a stranger named Strindler arrives in a small town in Arizona and requests money for providing the names of dead Mexican laborers. Adapted from the novel by Nikolai Gogol.

screenings.title: A Woman’s Torment
screenings.description: Don (Jeffrey Hurst) and his wife Frances (Crystal Sync) are struggling with their marriage—and Frances’s mentally ill live-in sister, Karen (Tara Chung), is the major reason why. When Tara overhears the unhappy couple talking about having her committed to an asylum one day, she runs away and takes refuge in an empty house on a remote beach. But she slowly begins to lose her grip on reality, giving way to increasingly violent delusions and an ever-growing bloodlust.

screenings.title: Mr. Jones
screenings.description: Holland’s razor-sharp thriller, set on the eve of world WWII, sees Hitler’s rise to power and Stalin’s Soviet propaganda machine pushing their “utopia” to the Western world. Meanwhile an ambitious young journalist, Gareth Jones (James Norton) travels to Moscow to uncover the truth behind the propaganda, but then gets a tip that could expose an international conspiracy, one that could cost him and his informant their lives. Jones goes on a life-or-death journey to uncover the truth behind the façade that would later inspire George Orwell’s seminal book Animal Farm. In English, Ukrainian, Russian and Welsh with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Taste of Streep presents: Mamma Mia!
Click | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: A harried workaholic, Michael Newman (Adam Sandler) doesn’t have time for his wife (Kate Beckinsale) and children, not if he’s to impress his ungrateful boss and earn a well-deserved promotion. So when he meets Morty (Christopher Walken), a loopy sales clerk, he gets the answer to his prayers: a magical remote that allows him to bypass life’s little distractions with increasingly hysterical results. But as Michael gleefully mutes, skips and scans past his family and his friends, the remote gradually takes over his life and begins to program him, in this fast, funny and out-of-control comedy adventure.

screenings.title: Fat City
screenings.description: Huston made a potent return to form after a string of critical and box office disappointments. Fat City sees him taking on Leonard Gardner’s screenplay adaptation of his own novel. An unvarnished view of boxing unfolds, as seen from the cheaper seats and fought from the lower depths, while comer Jeff Bridges scales the ring card and seasoned Stacy Keach may be on his way down. Also featuring Candy Clark in her film debut and an Oscar-nominated Susan Tyrrell. The result is Huston’s first unequivocal success in the New Hollywood era.

screenings.title: Zachariah
screenings.description: Firepower meets flower power in this outrageous western about two thrill-seeking cowboys who rock the range. Starring John Rubinstein (THE CAR), Don Johnson (TV’s MIAMI VICE), and Dick Van Patten (HIGH ANXIETY) and featuring legendary musicians Country Joe and the Fish and White Lightnin’, this psychedelic trip through the Wild West is an utterly unique film experience. Two cowboys (Rubinstein and Johnson) set out for adventure and join up with a band of rock ‘n’ roll outlaws. But as the two friends are seduced by their own quick-draw ambitions, a deadly rivalry grows between them, and they must struggle to find a path to peace – before they lose more than their reputations…and kill more than their friendship. Hollywood veteran George Englund (THE UGLY AMERICAN) directed this one-of-a-kind cult classic.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Girl 6
screenings.description: Perhaps Spike Lee’s most underrated film, and currently out of print on home media, Girl 6 was the first film that Spike directed without also writing the screenplay. Pulitzer Prize winning playwright Suzan-Lori Parks (Topdog/Underdog) takes the screenwriting reigns here as we follow Judy (played to perfection by Teresa Randle, in what should have been a star-making performance), who on her journey to become an famous actress finds herself utilizing her performance skills as a phone sex operator.

screenings.title: Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass
screenings.description: Small town hairdresser Gail Daughtry is engaged to her devoted high school sweetheart, Tom. Her life takes a turn when a trip to a book signing leads to Tom meeting – and sleeping – with his “celebrity pass”. Reeling from the betrayal, Gail impulsively joins her friend Otto on a trip to Los Angeles, where a psychic convinces Gail that the only way to save her marriage is to “even the scales” with her own celebrity pass: Jon Hamm. Thus begins an epic journey through Tinseltown as Gail and Otto join forces with a talent agency assistant, a paparazzo, and actor John Slattery, all in the search for Hamm. Along the way, they collide with celebrities and are hunted by a group of Italian assassins as they get ever closer to finding the elusive star.

screenings.title: Taste of Streep presents: Mamma Mia!
Characters Disappearing
screenings.description: New York City, 1971. As Mei, Chris and Leonard trace differing paths through this melancholic vision of the Asian American Movement, collective paranoia rises as those around them begin to vanish without explanation.

screenings.title: Future Future
screenings.description: [FUTURO FUTURO]In a bleak near-future Brazil where artificial intelligence has triggered a mysterious neurological crisis, K is a forty-year-old man who has lost both his memory and sense of belonging. Drifting through a desolate unnamed city, shaped by deepening social inequality and technological control, he embarks on an absurd and increasingly tragic search for identity and connection. Blending dystopian science fiction with political allegory, director Davi Pretto’s fourth feature crafts a formally daring vision of a collapsing society haunted by environmental catastrophe, class divisions, and the dehumanizing promises of technological progress. Incorporating artificial intelligence into its own visual language, the film is a hypnotic and cautionary portrait of a world that feels both eerily distant and unsettlingly close.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Deadlock
screenings.description: A young man, Kid, stumbles through the Mexican Sierra, shot and half bled to death, carrying a suitcase containing the loot from a bank robbery. Passing out from heat and blood loss, he is found by Charles Dump, a former gold miner living on the outskirts of the ghost town “Deadlock” with his daughter (Klick discovery Mascha Elm-Rabben, later to appear in Werner Schroeter’s BOMBERPILOT and SALOME, and Fassbinder’s WORLD ON A WIRE). As Dump realizes what’s in the suitcase, he tries to come up with a plan to get rid of its owner. As they are joined by Kid’s partner in crime, the sadistic killer Sunshine, the conflict triangle is perfect. Soon it’s everyone for himself in a violent endgame under the glistening sun where only one can walk away with the suitcase. DEADLOCK is a dark, nihilistic tale of greed, corruption and codes of honor. A chamber play of Beckettian proportions, it is also a psychedelic Western as gritty as they come. Boasting admirers ranging from Jodorowsky to Spielberg to Tarantino, DEADLOCK is graced with a soundtrack by legendary Krautrock band CAN.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Ec: Joseph Cornell
screenings.description: Unless otherwise noted, all the films in this program are silent. With the exception of GNIR REDNOW, all films have been preserved by Anthology Film Archives.ROSE HOBART (ca. 1936/68, 20 min, 16mm, sound. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives. Brand-new print!)CENTURIES OF JUNE (1955, 10 min, 16mm. Photographed by Stan Brakhage.)THE AVIARY (1954, 11 min, 16mm. Photographed by Rudy Burckhardt.)GNIR REDNOW (1955, 5 min, 16mm. Photographed by Stan Brakhage.)NYMPHLIGHT (1957, 8 min, 16mm. Photographed by Rudy Burckhardt.)A LEGEND FOR FOUNTAINS (1957/65, 17 min, 16mm. Photographed by Rudy Burckhardt; completed by Lawrence Jordan.)ANGEL (1957, 3 min, 16mm. Photographed by Rudy Burckhardt.)“[ROSE HOBART] is a breathtaking example of the potential for surrealistic imagery within a conventional Hollywood film once it is liberated from its narrative causality. […] In Cornell’s later films – both those photographed by Rudy Burckhardt, Stan Brakhage, and Larry Jordan and the collage films which Jordan completed – Joseph Cornell describes the marginal area where the conscious and the unconscious meet. These are films which affirm a sustained present moment in which a quality of reminiscence is implicated.” –P. Adams Sitney, VISIONARY FILMTotal running time: ca. 80 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Mad Dog Morgan
screenings.description: “One of the key movies in the birth of the Australian film industry, MAD DOG MORGAN is as wild, free, and untamed as the pioneer Australian settler turned outlaw it celebrates. Dan Morgan was a real-life figure, a desperado who roamed the bush, committing robberies, drinking rum, killing people at the slightest provocation and generally behaving like a maniac. Obviously not just anyone could play the role, so director Philippe Mora brought in the only actor who could embody Morgan’s peculiar brand of apeshit craziness: Dennis Hopper. Hopper was dead-on perfect for Morgan but, unfortunately for the sanity of the cast and crew, he was also a committed method actor who insisted on getting into the role by drinking at least as much rum as the real Morgan and carrying loaded weapons everywhere. At one point during the shoot Hopper drunkenly took off in a car to visit the real Morgan’s grave. He was picked up in the state of Victoria for drunken driving. When his blood alcohol content was measured he was declared legally dead. His producers got him out of jail but he was forbidden by the court to drive or even to be a passenger in a car in the territory!” –Lars NilsenCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: La Notte

His misery weighs heavily on his wife, Lidia (Jeanne Moreau), already carrying her own cargo of existential anguish. In the course of a day and a night—spent at a hospital sickroom, a book launch, a nightclub, and a party at an industrialist’s villa, where Giovanni flirts extensively with the host’s daughter, Valentina (Monica Vitti)—the couple must come to terms with the extinction of the love that once existed between them… or not? A film steeped in despair but thrilling in its adventurous, architectonic use of the cinematic medium, from its opening credits—an avant-jazz/musique concrète overture accompanying the industrialized Milanese cityscape—to its beguiling final scene.

screenings.description: Followed by a Q&A with director Lucía Garibaldi Dir. Lucia Garibaldi. 2025, 96 mins. Uruguay/Argentina. In Spanish with English subtitles. This boundary-pushing, visually arresting sci-fi drama is the highly anticipated second feature from Uruguayan filmmaker Lucía Garibaldi (a Sundance Best Director winner for The Sharks). Set in a bleak, out-of-time neighborhood where routine fumigations mask a sinister reality, the film follows 18-year-old Elisa (Martina Passeggi in a breakthrough performance), the last young person in her community selected for a mysterious journey to the “North”—a distant promised land from where no one has ever returned. Grounding her film in a deeply personal story, Garibaldi creates a stylized, dystopian reality not far from our own—where youth is currency, ants are malevolent, and dogs are extinct—to explore intergenerational sacrifice and the definitive power of refusal. Ray [works] in terrain perhaps more familiar to Cassavetes… Selfish men and their hopes and cruelties and spectacular lack of wisdom. Women who see through them. The great Soumitra Chatterjee: lost but searching. The great Sharmila Tagore: mysterious, cerebral, mesmerizing. From the master, another masterpiece.” —Wes Anderson

Though it’s one of the most frequently adapted works in the history of cinema, William Shakespeare’s Hamlet had never been filmed in its complete unabridged version—until Kenneth Branagh went about the task for this lavish, star-studded 1996 production. Set within the vast, cold interiors of a vaguely 19th-century manor, this magnificent adaptation stars Branagh as the melancholy son of the Danish court, along with a Who’s Who of late 20th-century master thespians, including Christie, Jacobi, Dench, Depardieu, Gielgud, and a young Winslet as the aggrieved Ophelia, all captured in sumptuous 70mm. A dazed Yankee Civil War soldier (played by Downey) mysteriously awakens in early-1960s NYC where, naturally, he heads to Yankee Stadium; Alan Abel, Director of the Society for Indecency to Naked Animals (SINA), speaks from the heart of his group’s moral crusade to clothe all animals; Charles J. Guiteau repeatedly bungles his assassination attempts on President James Garfield; a priestly pervert and a chimp (yes, a chimp) engage with a plus-sized lover; and, in what just might be the most disorienting portion, Downey visits the seriously swinging singles scene that is the original T.G.I. Friday’s on the Upper East Side. screenings.description: A young man, Kid, stumbles through the Mexican Sierra, shot and half bled to death, carrying a suitcase containing the loot from a bank robbery. Passing out from heat and blood loss, he is found by Charles Dump, a former gold miner living on the outskirts of the ghost town “Deadlock” with his daughter (Klick discovery Mascha Elm-Rabben, later to appear in Werner Schroeter’s BOMBERPILOT and SALOME, and Fassbinder’s WORLD ON A WIRE). As Dump realizes what’s in the suitcase, he tries to come up with a plan to get rid of its owner. As they are joined by Kid’s partner in crime, the sadistic killer Sunshine, the conflict triangle is perfect. Soon it’s everyone for himself in a violent endgame under the glistening sun where only one can walk away with the suitcase. DEADLOCK is a dark, nihilistic tale of greed, corruption and codes of honor. A chamber play of Beckettian proportions, it is also a psychedelic Western as gritty as they come. Filled with interviews and truly outrageous archival footage, this immensely charming documentary is a true family film made by their daughter, Jenny and her husband, Jeff Hockett. They provide a rollicking first-hand account of what it was like growing up with professional prankster parents. Alan worked tirelessly to plant insane stories in the news and was never afraid to go to ridiculous lengths in order to expose what he believed to be an injustice. ABEL RAISES CAIN takes the audience on an up-close tour of the many elaborate schemes that he pulled off over the years, all designed to provoke, amuse, and prod people to question everything that they see and believe.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!
